title: Federal Register: Certificates of Compliance, final rule (eFiling) with Final Regulatory Flexibility Analysis

history.reason: Source read directly on the access date (PDF from GovInfo converted with pdftotext); findings transcribed from the document.

publisher: U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission (via GovInfo / Federal Register)
source_type: Government final rule with final regulatory flexibility analysis
reliability: Government document; the issuing agency (CPSC) is also the party administering the requirement. Estimates are the Commission's own.
findings: The final rule requires importers to eFile certificates (CPCs for children's products) with Customs at entry; CPSC treats cost above one percent of revenue as economically significant for small firms.
CPSC estimates the rule applies to about 230,000 small firms for children's products (18,852 manufacturers and 211,148 importers).

CPSC estimates average startup cost for eFiling of $1,086 per firm (about 20 hours), which it deems nonsignificant for the typical small firm, and says commenters offered no specific data on technology investment sizes.

CPSC estimates the average cost of the rule per small importer of children's products at $1,099 a year, below the roughly $10,000 one-percent threshold it computes for firms with about $1 million revenue, and about $72.28 per CPC eFiling in the first year (0.5999 percent of estimated revenue per certificate).
The rule states the domestic manufacturers are unaffected by eFiling.
limitations: Covers the certificate filing layer only (not lab testing); first-year and annualized figures differ and only some were read.
Ex ante agency estimates; the rule's effective dates and any later changes were not checked.
